About the role

We are recruiting a Building Maintenance Surveyor to join the Operations and Maintenance team in Crawley Homes. This key technical role supports the delivery of high-quality repairs, maintenance and improvement works across our housing stock and associated buildings.

As a Building Maintenance Surveyor, you will be responsible for the day-to-day responsive repairs and programmed inspection, diagnosis and management of building maintenance work across an allocated area. This includes domestic housing, leasehold properties, sheltered accommodation, hostels and public buildings.

You will:

carry out property inspections, surveys and defect diagnosis
prepare drawings, specifications and cost estimates
supervise contractors and administer building contracts
certify works and payments and manage quality on site
deal with customer enquiries, complaints and disrepair claims
support asset data updates and statutory compliance
work closely with housing officers, contractors and stakeholders

You may also cover void inspections, urgent works in other areas, mutual exchange reports and Sanctuary Scheme inspections when required.

What we are looking for

We are seeking an experienced, customer-focused surveyor who can work under pressure, manage multiple workstreams and communicate effectively with tenants, leaseholders, contractors and colleagues.

Essential requirements include:

strong building inspection and defect diagnosis skills across multiple trades
ability to prepare specifications, drawings and cost estimates
knowledge of housing repairs, maintenance and planned works
understanding of health & safety, building regulations and relevant legislation
good IT skills, including works ordering and asset management systems
full current UK driving licence 

Qualifications / Experience:

RICS or CIOB building surveying certificate or working towards it
relevant construction, building surveying or property qualification
experience in building maintenance, repairs and contract supervision
budgetary control and certification experience

Experience in local authority or housing association maintenance and working within partnering contracts is desirable.

Why join Crawley Homes?

You’ll be joining a team committed to maintaining and improving homes, placing customers at the heart of the service, and supporting professional development within a collaborative environment.

Additional information

Satisfactory clearance of a Basic Disclosure and Barring Service check (DBS) will be a condition of employment. 

Essential car user car allowance (currently under review).

Occasional out-of-hours working may be required.

A full and current UK driving licence will be a requirement of the role.

Crawley is a great place to work, with a thriving business district and excellent transport connections including nearby Gatwick Airport. We are based in our modern Town Hall which opened in 2023 and is located a short walk from the town centre and railway station.

Employee benefits

We offer a generous employee benefits package, with a range of discounts, benefits and wellbeing incentives to suit everyone.

At Crawley Borough Council, you will have access to a structured programme of learning from day one, designed to help you succeed in your role and grow your career.

Local government reorganisation

Local government reorganisation (LGR) is planned across Sussex, with new unitary authorities expected by 2028. While this represents a significant change for councils, most roles will continue to focus on delivering vital services to our residents and business communities. As the future structure evolves, our name may change, but our commitment to providing excellent services and supporting our employees will not. Joining us now means being part of a dedicated team during an important and evolving time for local government.

Our way of working

Our shared values and behaviours reflect the special nature of our council. We encourage all colleagues to put them into practice, whatever job they do. Take a look to see if we are the perfect match.

Safer recruitment

Crawley Borough Council is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and vulnerable adults and expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment. We want to be an inclusive and diverse employer of first choice reflecting the community we serve and particularly welcome applications from all under represented groups.

How to apply

Click the Apply button to complete your application online. Please ensure that the reference details you supply are for your current or most recent employer and that any gaps in employment are covered on your application form. Please note that CVs will not be accepted without a fully completed application form.

For more information about the role, please contact james.farncombe@crawley.gov.uk, Senior Building Maintenance Surveyor.

We recommend that you submit your application as soon as possible, as we may close this advert before the stated closing date if enough applications are received.

title: Business Support & Operations Administrator
description:
About Lenmark

Lenmark Construction Ltd is an established, family-run groundworks and civil engineering company. Having grown steadily over the years, we are delighted to be expanding our strong, energetic office team.

We pride ourselves on our friendly, supportive working environment, where everyone works together and plays an important part in the success of the business.

We are looking for a highly motivated, organised and enthusiastic individual to join our team in a varied role supporting finance, purchasing, training and general business operations.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys working with numbers, is confident using Excel and technology, and likes finding better and more efficient ways of working.

The Role

Working closely with our Finance Director and wider office team, you will provide support across several areas of the business, including finance, purchasing, training, operational systems and general administration.

This is a flexible and varied position, where priorities may change depending on the needs of the business. You will have the opportunity to work alongside different departments, gain an understanding of how the company operates and gradually take on additional responsibilities.

We are particularly interested in finding someone who enjoys problem-solving, embraces new technology and can help us continue improving the way we work.

Key Responsibilities

Finance, Excel & Reporting

Assist the Finance Director with financial administration, spreadsheets and reporting.
Prepare, maintain and analyse Excel spreadsheets and financial data.
Assist with producing financial and operational reports.
Check information, reconcile figures and investigate discrepancies.
Support ongoing improvements to financial processes and reporting.

Purchasing & Supplier Support

Assist the purchasing team with routine orders, including PPE, consumables and general site requirements.
Place purchase orders, carry out online ordering and liaise with suppliers.
Monitor pricing, order progress and deliveries to ensure goods arrive within required timescales.
Maintain accurate purchasing records and follow up outstanding orders.
Develop knowledge of the purchasing function, with the opportunity to take on more responsibility as experience and confidence grow.

Systems, Technology & Business Improvements

Help maintain and update internal systems, including Monday.com and Construction Manager.
Assist with implementing new software and improving existing systems and processes.
Support colleagues with system updates, data accuracy and day-to-day administration.
Explore opportunities to use AI, automation and technology to improve efficiency.
Help identify ways to streamline processes, reduce unnecessary administration and improve how information is managed across the business.

Training & General Business Support

Assist with organising employee training and maintaining training records.
Help keep the company training matrix accurate and up to date.
Liaise with employees, managers and training providers regarding upcoming courses and requirements.
Provide flexible administrative support across different departments, helping colleagues with workloads, deadlines and ongoing projects.
Assist with general office administration and ad-hoc tasks as required.

What We Need From You

Strong Excel skills, confidence working with figures and a logical, analytical approach.
Excellent organisational skills and the ability to prioritise a varied workload.
Good IT skills, including Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and Outlook.
Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
A proactive, resourceful attitude and the confidence to use your own initiative.
An interest in technology, AI and improving business processes.
The ability to learn new systems quickly and adapt to different tasks.
Good written and verbal communication skills.
The ability to work independently and as part of a team.
A flexible, hands-on approach and willingness to support colleagues across the business.

Experience & Skills

Previous experience in an administrative, finance, purchasing or operational support role would be beneficial.

Experience working with spreadsheets, reports and financial information is particularly desirable.

Knowledge of the construction industry, purchasing processes or business management software would be an advantage, but is not essential, as training will be provided.

We are more interested in finding someone with the right attitude, strong organisational skills and the ability to learn and develop.

The Opportunity

This is not a role limited to one department or a fixed set of tasks. You will become an integral part of our office team, supporting different areas of the business and helping to keep things running smoothly.

As your knowledge of the company develops, there will be opportunities to take greater ownership of tasks, particularly within purchasing, systems and business administration.

We are looking for someone who enjoys being busy, takes pride in their work and wants to contribute ideas and improvements as the business continues to grow.

As Cemeteries and Allotments Assistant your main focus will be to support our Allotments Officer in the upkeep and maintenance of our 20 allotment sites. In addition, you will be working as part of a small team responsible for the day-to-day operation of both cemetery sites.

Duties at the allotment sites will include:

strimming
grass cutting 
clearance of plots
repairs and maintenance within the communal areas
meeting contractors for repairs or maintenance including compliance checks

Duties at the cemeteries will include:

compassion for families and friends of the deceased
marking out

Therefore, it would be advantageous if you have proven experience of using plant machinery, hedge cutters, strimmer and ride on mowers.

The successful candidate will need experience of operating this equipment, relevant certification, or a willingness to undertake training and gain certification within six months of the agreed start date.

You will also need to be confident driving the allotments tipper truck and trailer, training dependant. Our current fleet is 3.5 tonne Vauxhall Movano tipper with towing capability.

You will need to have very good verbal communication skills and a high degree of emotional intelligence and empathy to deal with customers and the public appropriately.

In return, we offer the exciting opportunity to be part of a dedicated team providing excellent cemetery and allotment provision, excellent working conditions and pension scheme.

You will need to be comfortable working alone and as part of a team when undertaking the daily duties.

Additional information

Required to participate as part of a standby rota for Saturday burials, for which an additional payment is made.

A full, current UK Category B driving licence, held for a minimum of one year, will be a requirement of the role.

Satisfactory clearance of a basic disclosure and barring service (DBS) check will be a condition of employment.

description:
Salary: £25,550 to £27,000 – (dependent on experience)

Contract Type: Permanent and Fixed Term Contract roles available

Security Level: BPSS

Location: Aviation House, Gatwick – 2 days office attendance per week.

Visa Restrictions: This position does not offer visa sponsorship

 

Closing Date: Wednesday 28th October 2026

Assessment Centre Dates: Tuesday 10th & Wednesday 11th November (at our Aviation House, Gatwick Head Office)

 

We are the UK's aviation and aerospace regulator and recognised as a world leader in its field. Our activities are diverse, enabling the aviation industry to meet the highest safety standards, and we pride ourselves on our ability to adapt to the constantly evolving aviation environment.

 

The Shared Service Centre (SSC) at the Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) provides a range of services that underpin the UK’s Aviation Safety framework and is the starting point for so many CAA processes where the first line of regulatory control and safety regulation begins at the application stage. We handle the applications for most of the licences, certificates, approvals, permits and permissions that the CAA issues. 

  

The Role 

  

Our comprehensive on the job training means you'll need to be flexible – processing different types of applications and information, dealing with telephone queries, managing emails and learning about all aspects of the SSC and its' services all the while making sure excellent customer service is at the heart of everything you do. 

You'll be surprised at the technical expertise, insight, and knowledge you can learn on the job and in time, find yourself advising and guiding others on specialist subjects. 

  

About You 

  

We need people who are great team players with a collaborative approach, able to work in an environment of change and are comfortable with switching focus depending on workload demands. As this is a high-paced environment, you will need to be proactive, not afraid of challenges and willing to go the extra mile to ensure the delivery of tasks and deadlines are met. 

  

IT skills in a range of Microsoft packages and using bespoke databases and systems are essential as well as the ability to communicate clearly and professionally, both verbally and in writing. You will need to be conscientious in your own work with an emphasis on quality and high standards, as well as having an eye for detail when checking and reviewing documentation received into the department. Previous experience of working in a customer service or aviation related setting would be an advantage but not essential. 

  

What Can We Offer You? 

  

We are focused on the development of our people, and you will have the opportunity to work alongside creative and collaborative team members who are keen to make a difference to the CAA. 

 

We offer a hybrid working arrangement however successful candidates will be required to attend training onsite in the Gatwick office for approximately the first 12 weeks of their employment. 

 

Additional Information

 

For many appointments within the CAA, these roles require access to operationally sensitive infrastructure and/or Nationally Protected information. For these roles the post holders must undergo National Security Vetting and achieve the appropriate level of clearance.

 

BPSS - To be vetted you must have the right to work in the UK so that meaningful checks can be undertaken.

 

If you do not meet these requirements, we may not be able to accept your application.

 

For more information on BPSS clearance please visit - BPSS clearance

 

The CAA values high ethical standards and personal integrity among employees. If invited for interview you will be asked to complete a declaration of interest.

 

Relocation & Property


The CAA will be relocating from Aviation House (Our Gatwick Office) to new premises in a few years’ time. Our move is driven by strategic, operational and environmental considerations.

 

We will be moving to a new local home, up to a 15-mile radius of Aviation House, to minimise disruption for our valued colleagues and customers.

 

We are now working with colleagues and visitors to understand what we need in our new office, before we start our property search. We will sell Aviation House and land, vacate the site and move to new premises, but we do not expect to move before 2028

 

Inclusive Recruitment

 

We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome applications from all backgrounds. As a Disability Confident employer, candidates who meet the minimum requirements will be guaranteed an interview. Find out more about the Disability Confident Scheme. If you require any adjustments during the recruitment process, please let us know.


Use of Artificial Intelligence by candidates in the CAA recruitment process

 

We recognise that many of our candidates find Artificial Intelligence to be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be rejected on that basis.

 

Working With Us

 

Explore What We Offer section on our careers website to find out about our benefits and how we support work-life balance.


Our Values


Do The Right Thing, Never Stop Learning, Build Collaborative Relationships, Respect Everyone – For more information please Click Here


Closing Date: Wednesday 28th October 2026

Assessment Centre Dates: Tuesday 10th & Wednesday 11th November (at our Aviation House, Gatwick Head Office)

We are seeking a motivated and dynamic individual to lead a Programme Administration team, providing key administrative support and record maintenance for a specified portfolio of courses, in accordance with the procedures and regulations of UAL.
Based at London College of Fashion’s Eastbank site, you will manage a team of Programme Administrators, overseeing the provision of relevant administrative support for all courses within your portfolio of programmes, ensuring an excellent and high-quality service delivery and a seamless student experience, from the point of enrolment through to graduation.
A key part of the role will involve working alongside academics with essential tasks such as monitoring student attendance, exam boards and assessments, course documentation as well as quality processes.

About you

The ideal candidate will have experience in key aspects of Further or Higher Education student administration, including registry processes such as enrolment and assessment.
You will have an enthusiasm for creating a good student experience and be able to evidence strong leadership and line-management skills, with the ability to set clear objectives and motivate your team.
You will be organised and able to plan a busy workload, communicating with colleagues in your team and key stakeholders. 

If you have any general questions or have accessibility needs, please contact AGstaffrecruitment@arts.ac.uk
Application process 
We operate a fair and open anonymous selection process. Thus, you will need to create an account and submit an application through our job board. As part of this, you will need to provide a supporting statement to demonstrate your suitability. Our recruitment process involves: application, shortlisting, assessment/interview, offer, onboarding.

We understand the benefits of using AI in work. But, if you are thinking of using it to submit an application, we ask you to think about what value it adds. AI tools tend to lack the personal touch and authenticity we value in candidates. We encourage you to showcase your unique knowledge and skills using your own voice.

We encourage you to apply as soon as possible as this vacancy may close early if we receive a high level of interest. We will aim to give at least 24 hours' notice of any changes to the closing date.
